successors.name: Republic of India
successors.text: Tripura: the hill kingdom of the Manikya kings (the princely state of Hill Tippera)

ledger.x: c. 1400: the Kingdom page's infobox gives 'c. 1400-15 October 1949'; the princely-state page has Maha Manikya ascending in 1400 (the Manikya title dates from this king). The page names the land only as the hill kingdom of Twipra; Tripura's modern boundary is drawn.
Dhanya Manikya 'expanded Twipra's territorial domain well into Eastern Bengal'.
1562: 'Chilarai attacked the kingdom and took possession of the Barak Valley'; Khaspur became a Koch dewani.
1733: 'Mughal dominance of the plains of the kingdom'.

1764: 'when the British East India Company took control of Bengal' the Mughal-held parts of Bengal passed to British administration; the page does not mention Tripura's lowlands again, and the kings kept only the Chakla Roshnabad estate (1,476 km2), a landlord's holding rather than a state's land.
1905: Tripura 'joined Eastern Bengal and Assam as Hill Tippera'.
15 October 1949: the state merges into the Union of India as a Part C State.

wars.name: Koch conquest of the Barak Valley
wars.outcome: Chilarai's Koch army took the Barak Valley from Tripura; Khaspur became a Koch dewani.

certainty.note: A hill kingdom with no surveyed frontier; the Eastern Bengal plains, Sylhet, the Chittagong Hill Tracts and the Barak Valley are bridged lands.
The hill state's frontier is drawn as the modern state of Tripura; the princely state's area (10,660 km2 in 1941) is about 10 percent larger than the grid shape.
